newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo's Gyll says vehicle business strong.
newsitem.headline: Volvo's Gyll says vehicle business strong.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday its poor operating profit for the first nine months of the year did not reflect the group's position as a vehicle maket.

"The weak operating profit...does not reflect the group's strategic position. Both Volvo Car and Volvo Truck now have a highly competitive product range," Volvo CEO Soren Gyll said in comments on the group's nine-month results.
Volvo's main task is to increase productivity and improve cost-efficiency, Gyll said.
Volvo posted a 12 percent rise in nine-month pre-tax profits to 12.03 billion crowns even though sales slipped 12 percent to 113.64 billion.
However operating profit slumped to 2.32 billion crowns from 8.84 billion in the same period last year.
The sale of the company's shareholding in U.S./Swedish drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn provided a capital gain of 7.8 billion crowns.
